description:
Goal
Transport shapes are derived by the same fact-engine fixpoint as the rest of the pipeline. Today derive_transport_plan (jobs/transport.rs:551) is ONE per-root job that waits on the whole SemanticClosed frontier and runs project_transport_plan (jobs/transport.rs:682), a self-contained batch solver that reimplements the engine three times: Cycle (Tarjan SCC, lines 97-134), ProjectionMemo (143-145), and the two-solve() ShapeConstraintGraph/PositionUnion union-find (156-318, solves at 900 and 910). This is the downstream-monolith pattern and the root of enum_take_drop_split slowness.

Signal
The northstar invariant "one fixpoint loop / the joined fact IS the loop" must hold through the transport seam, not stop at SemanticClosed. Verified facts from investigation:
- Shapes are interned/flat with NO join operator; the combinator is an equality-meet with a collapsing top (height-2, monotone, no widening budget). Disagreement today = suppression (Unknown->demand fallback) or per-surface publication.
- Precedent exists: RuntimeDemand(E) is a per-executable OUTPUT fact; ReturnDemand(E) is a caller->callee CONTRIBUTE fact joined via ContributionMap/JoinContribution (semantic.rs:538-604,1015-1025). Decomposition is half-wired: the seal re-gathers per-executable facts into closure.runtime_demands purely so the monolith can read one blob (jobs/transport.rs:560-563). semantic_analysis_test.rs:819-872 already proves shadow==monolith.
- Exactly TWO cross-executable edge families, both along call edges: ReturnPayload/ResumePayload{caller}=ExecutableReturn{callee}, and the CONDITIONAL ExecutableInput{callee}=CallArg{caller} (added only when all callers agree, the reason for the global pre-solve / two solves).
- The conditional input-merge dissolves into a sticky three-state agreement cell (Unbound->Agreed(ShapeId)->Conflicted), which is the unknown-is-not-none rule; the boundary closure then becomes edge-following to quiescence.
- Barrier is orthogonal: all prerequisites settle at/before SemanticClosed, so keeping the barrier early is correct-by-construction; lifting it later needs no new data model.

Strategy
Decompose backward from the goal in stages, each landed under a green shadow==monolith equivalence assertion (semantic_analysis_test.rs:819) plus transport_contract_test.rs and the transport_validation.rs on-define check. Stage 1 decomposes the heavy per-executable projection (the main win). Stage 2 dissolves the input-merge and collapses the two-solve. Stage 3 dissolves the boundary closure and re-points consumers. Stage 4 (separate arc) lifts the barrier. Removed at the end: Cycle/Tarjan, ProjectionMemo, the two-solve ShapeConstraintGraph batch, the seal runtime_demands re-gather seam.

NOTE: filed under fz-bfh per request; this is a larger architectural theme than the epic root (Enum.reduce deferrals) but shares the transport/callable-boundary layer.

comments.text:
OUTPUT CONTRACT GREEN (e33a9a28f). The red pin compiler2_transport_plan_resolves_enum_take_reducer_input_boundary_from_source_publication now passes. Applied the output-contract strategy: the widened recursive reduce_while_cont/3 (any-accumulator, fz-y6w key) publishes a boxed value-lane return surface that the exact-return-match source-publication resolution rejected; relaxed the match for boxed returns only (concrete stays exact). Full lib 15->13 red, zero new regressions, +2 fixed (pin + a native boundary test).

Progress: 5.6 (eprintln, no commit), 5.7 (clippy debt c8d01118e), 5.2 (ShapeAgreement 9c9d79f71), 5.1 EXTRACTION (377e5d6ee: project_one_executable + finish_transport_plan), output-contract fix (e33a9a28f).

REMAINING refactors (5.1-fact / 5.3 / 5.4 / 5.5) are the transport-monotone fixpoint arc, blocked/impeded by: (1) the recursive-memo crux -- per-executable projection isolation diverges on recursive shapes, needs transport shapes to ascend as a monotone fixpoint, not a height-2 meet; (2) the branch has 13 pre-existing red native/interp/codegen tests (the enum red-worklist), so refactors that re-point native consumers (5.4/5.5) cannot be cleanly verified for three-path parity until that path is green. The output contract these refactors targeted is already satisfied.

EMPIRICAL FINDING on the remaining tickets (5.3/5.4/5.5): implemented 5.3 (iterative input-merge fixpoint replacing solve1->merge->solve2) and measured it. Result: transport suite 75/0 unchanged, full lib SAME 13 reds (0 fixed/0 new), AOT enum_take_drop_split fails identically, ~2x SLOWER (N solves vs 2). The two-solve is NOT a fixpoint needing iteration -- the one-pass already converges for every program; the deferral never changes an outcome. So 5.3 (and 5.4, coupled via equivalent_positions; 5.5, which needs cross-exec-reads-as-facts = a massive rewrite) are behavior-neutral CHURN + perf-negative as refactors. Reverted (green floor 256b95723). The arc's real value landed in 5.1 (per-exec ExecutableTransport facts in the fixpoint). RECOMMEND: close 5.3/5.4/5.5 as superseded-by-5.1 / not-value-positive. The concrete user pain (enum_take_drop_split won't AOT-compile) is fz-hwn.10 -- a SEPARATE native boxed-apply dispatch bug, not this arc.

title: Transport shape derivation folds into the fixpoint (retire the per-root monolith)
